title: Airport, 5:30 AM
excerpt: The airport is a magical place.
content:
The airport is a magical place.

People meet and part, sprint and wait. Look—there’s a man with a guitar, adding a silent background track to his own journey. There’s another with a bouquet, glancing around, wondering when his luck will finally land. And someone else, lugging a massive suitcase and buying a neck pillow, perhaps waking up on the other side of the ocean.

Fates intertwine, then sever. This is likely the first time you’ll brush shoulders with him, and the last. These fleeting encounters create a peculiar energy field, one that allows me to detach from my "subject" self and observe—inward or outward—as an "object."

Step through the gate, put on the eye mask, pick a random loading animation, and let your memories save. Don't fear the turbulence; it’s just the new terrain loading.

"Could I have a coffee, please?" I wonder if this flicker of heart palpitations is from the caffeine or the anticipation of seeing a new flame—or an old love. Then I realize: it’s the greedy timeline stretching out, rooting itself like a tree into every corner of the universe. That feeling of weightlessness? That’s me falling into a new abyss of time. I didn't jump; I slipped. How could I ever be prepared, especially when met by that gentle, drowsy voice asking, "Chicken rice or pasta?"

My thorned time capsule rests quietly outside the window. The bold print on its manual—"PIT 6:00 AM"—reminds me that this abyss is one I dove into of my own volition.

"What could be wrong" has become my mantra lately. I can always find a reason to do something.

So I wait, then I run. Once I find a reason I truly believe in, I set off.

A new journey begins.
